title: Database Connection Error
description: Resolve 'Error establishing a database connection' — wrong credentials, down MySQL server, or corrupted wp-config.

steps.title: Confirm Site-Wide Database Failure
steps.instructions: If only one page fails, it may be a plugin query issue — not a true connection error. True DB errors block the entire site including wp-admin.

steps.title: Check MySQL/MariaDB Server Status
steps.instructions: Verify the database service is running in hosting panel. Check for host maintenance notices or resource limit suspensions.

steps.title: Verify wp-config.php Credentials
steps.instructions: Confirm DB_NAME, DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD, and DB_HOST match hosting credentials. After migration, host may use a socket path instead of localhost.

steps.title: Test Connection Outside WordPress
steps.instructions: Use phpMyAdmin, MySQL CLI, or a one-line PHP mysqli test with the same credentials. Isolate whether WordPress or the server is at fault.

steps.title: Check max_connections and Sleeping Queries
steps.instructions: Too many connections from a runaway plugin or missing persistent cache can exhaust MySQL max_connections. Kill long-running queries and restart MySQL if safe.

steps.title: Repair Corrupted Tables if Needed
steps.instructions: If logs show 'table is marked as crashed', run REPAIR TABLE via phpMyAdmin. Restore from backup if corruption is widespread.

steps.title: Verify Site and Admin Access
steps.instructions: Load homepage and wp-admin. Monitor for recurring connection errors and document any credential or host changes made.
